Before working on this, understand what this does. https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/pull/16736 Analyze the changes. I want to make follow up changes.

1. In LocationForm:223-226, 

Every request in this bulk-create batch gets the same referenceId. It was equally broken before, sure, but you were right here retyping the line — reference ids exist so you can map a failed sub-request back to the bed that caused it. With N identical ids, the error toasts (and any future result mapping) are useless. Use bed.name or the index, like LocationImport already does.


2. InvoiceChargeItemTitle:101-104

Each query created here uses the default non-silent error handling, so every failed dispense is sent to the global QueryCache handler (src/Utils/request/queryClient.ts:26-28). This hook then emits failed_to_load_medication_details as well; with multiple failed dispenses, users receive one global toast per request plus the aggregate toast. Suppress the per-query global toast (or remove the aggregate notification) so the error is reported only once.

I’d say, let’s switch back to what it was before. let’s keep using useQuery with batch request itself. i don’t want to change something that already works. actually this pr changes it to useQueries right. but out of scope of this pr. see what has changes and let’s revert it back, but just update to use new batch request.
I will rename the session, then read the PR.

## Proposed Changes

- Migrates batch API calls to use the new `useBatchRequest` hook
- Replaces hand-built batch payloads and their bespoke `error.cause.results` parsers with the `useBatchRequest` hook, so failed sub-requests get the shared global error handling. Requests are now declared with typed `ApiRoute` objects instead of interpolated URL strings.
- The invoice charge item title fetched dispenses through the batch endpoint as a read; it now uses `useQueries` with `medicationDispenseApi.get`, since the hook is mutation-only.
- Adds the upsert routes the questionnaire structured handlers needed, and removes the deprecated `batchApi`.

108. /**
109.  * Creates a TanStack Query compatible query function that reads many
110.  * resources in one batch request.
111.  *
112.  * Use this function for reads only. Use {@link useBatchRequest} for writes.
113.  *
114.  * The batch endpoint always gives a 200 status if the transaction is
115.  * successful. Each sub-request keeps its own status code in the `results`
116.  * array. So you must check `status_code` of each result before you use its
117.  * `data`.
118.  *
119.  * Set `silent` to `true` if the caller shows the error itself. If you do not,
120.  * the global error handler shows a message for the full batch.
121.  *
122.  * Example:
123.  * ```tsx
124.  * const { data } = useQuery({
125.  *   queryKey: ["medication_dispense_batch", ids],
126.  *   queryFn: batchQuery<MedicationDispenseRetrieve>(
127.  *     ids.map((id) => ({
128.  *       api: medicationDispenseApi.get,
129.  *       pathParams: { id },
130.  *       referenceId: id,
131.  *     })),
132.  *     { silent: true },
133.  *   ),
134.  *   enabled: ids.length > 0,
135.  * });
136.  * ```
137.  */
138. export function batchQuery<T = unknown>(
139.   requests: BatchQueryObject[],
140.   options?: { silent?: boolean },
141. ) {
142.   const body = buildBatchRequestBody(
143.     requests.map((request) => ({ ...request, body: {} })),
144.   );
145. 
146.   return async ({ signal }: { signal: AbortSignal }) => {
147.     const response = await query(batchRequestApi, {
148.       body,
149.       silent: options?.silent,
150.     })({ signal });
151. 
152.     return response as BatchRequestResponse<T>;
153.   };
154. }
